prize_parts.citation: For turning the ubiquitin-proteasome system into a chemically programmable tool: heterobifunctional degraders that induce proximity between a target protein and an E3 ligase.

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation converts a biological process, regulated protein turnover, into a defined chemical reaction: a small molecule forms a ternary complex and the target is ubiquitinated and destroyed. The mechanism is quantitative (cooperativity, linker geometry, ligase-ligand structure), it has been reproduced across many laboratories and many E3 ligases, and it gives biologists a general way to remove proteins acutely, which is useful well beyond drug discovery. The link to disease is concrete, since degraders are in late-stage trials and the thalidomide-cereblon mechanism explains an old clinical puzzle. Crews and Deshaies introduced the concept experimentally and Ciulli supplied the structural and chemical basis that made it general and drug-like.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. A three-name limit forces a choice between the PROTAC strand and the molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray and others), and whichever we choose leaves out real discoverers. There is also a maturity argument: no PROTAC is yet an approved drug, so clinical validation of the principle is incomplete. By comparison, base editing and nanopore sequencing have cleaner single-lineage attribution, and nanopore sequencing has years of routine deployment.

responses.point: Aqvist ranked base editing first and argued for a Liu, Komor, Gaudelli trio, noting that Nishida and Kondo have a legitimate but different claim; he also saw the PROTAC versus glue split as a hard choice.
responses.response: I agree that base editing is a very strong alternative and that the glue-versus-PROTAC allocation is the real weakness of B038. Where I differ is that I would still keep Liu alone for B011: Komor and Gaudelli were first authors of the two founding papers, but the platform design and the evolution programme were Liu's, and the Kondo/Nishida priority question grows if the prize names trainees. I would also want off-target and bystander deamination quantified more carefully before I treat B011 as fully mature. On B038 the mechanistic science has been confirmed by many groups, which to me outweighs the missing approval.

responses.point: Linke put nanopore sequencing first for its clear physical principle and a new capability, and ranked PROTACs only fifth, partly because clinical validation is still emerging and recognition may be premature.
responses.response: I accept that nanopores are mature and independently validated, and I ranked them in my top five. My reservation is the same attribution problem, with five credible founders (Deamer, Branton, Kasianowicz, Bayley, Akeson) and only three slots, so any trio omits a founder. On maturity I disagree with calling degraders premature: the chemical principle is not in doubt, and a prize recognises the discovery and its confirmed mechanism, not drug approval. The timing risk is real but smaller than you suggest, and the allocation problem is comparable in both fields.

responses.point: Aili ranked PROTACs first with the same trio, but noted that the cereblon glue strand is a distinct contribution and that his nanopore selection omits some founders.
responses.response: We are aligned on the trio, and I think we should be honest that the cereblon work (Handa, Ito) is a distinct discovery rather than a footnote. If the committee wants to credit it, it needs a second part and the three-person ceiling makes that costly. My view is that a citation framed around induced proximity through heterobifunctional degraders is defensible and keeps the discovery well defined, with the glue mechanism noted in the committee's background text.

responses.point: Sparr ranked phase separation first and lipid nanoparticles second, emphasising their physical-chemical grounding and, for LNPs, very large demonstrated impact.
responses.response: The LNP impact is undeniable, but I rank it lower because credit is spread across academic and industrial groups and the mRNA-modification prize of 2023 already covers much of the framing. For phase separation, I share your view that the core phenomenon is robust, but several members, including Linke and Aqvist, note the debate over which condensates are truly phase-separated. As an experimentalist I would want that resolved by quantitative measurement in cells before I rank it above degraders.

uncertainties: How to allocate credit between PROTAC and molecular-glue (cereblon) discoveries within three names, and whether a prize built on one strand is fair to the other.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug makes recognition premature compared with base editing or nanopores.
Whether Komor and Gaudelli should share a base-editing prize with Liu, and how to treat the independent Kondo/Nishida claim.
I am working from memory on the current clinical status of degraders and have not verified it.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My work on dNTP pools and replication fidelity is only thematically adjacent to degraders and base editing, and I have no personal or institutional tie to the named candidates.
